name: Pelikan Stormshell Anorak
description:
A pullover rain shell in muted teal with a half-zip neck and a single kangaroo pocket across the front. Pelikan uses a bonded three-layer membrane that is genuinely waterproof — not water-resistant, not splash-proof — waterproof, in the sustained Lake Michigan rain that comes in November and doesn't stop until March. The hood packs into the collar. Seams are taped. The cut is trim but not restrictive, designed to layer over a mid-weight fleece or sweater.

This is a Tier 3 outdoor brand that takes its technical specs seriously without charging Tier 5 prices. Teachers, researchers, urban cyclists, and anyone who commutes on foot knows this jacket. It's not flashy. It just works, every time.
what_it_says: You've done your research and you spend money on things that perform. You probably also have opinions about coffee.
story_hooks: Pelikan recently switched membrane suppliers and the new batch has a subtle flaw — it fails at exactly 48 hours of continuous rain exposure, which matters if you're living in it
A courier who disappeared was last seen in a teal Pelikan anorak; three people matching that description were spotted near the Port Authority that night
Someone has been leaving sealed waterproof packages inside the kangaroo pockets of Pelikan jackets at a specific resale shop — different packages, different jackets, every week

physical_description.visual_profile: A streamlined pullover anorak in muted teal with a clean, purposeful silhouette. The half-zip neck and packable hood create a minimalist aesthetic that reads as competent rather than fashionable. The single front kangaroo pocket breaks the symmetry subtly. Overall impression: reliable, unfussy, built for function in harsh climates.
physical_description.fit: Trim but accommodating—designed to layer comfortably over mid-weight insulation without excess fabric. The cut skims the torso without compression, allowing arm mobility for cycling or walking. Sleeve length reaches the wrist bone; torso length hits mid-hip.
physical_description.primary_material: Bonded three-layer technical membrane—outer shell is lightweight ripstop synthetic, bonded to moisture-wicking mid-layer and inner lining. Genuinely waterproof (not water-resistant). Seams fully taped.
physical_description.texture: Smooth to the touch with a subtle sheen from the technical coating. The ripstop weave creates fine texture visible up close. Hood and collar have a softer microfleece lining for comfort against skin.
physical_description.color_scheme: Muted teal (desaturated blue-green, evocative of Lake Michigan in winter). No contrasting trim or branding marks. Seams in matching thread.
closures: Half-zip at neck for ventilation and layering access
Packable hood stows into collar via integrated drawcord
Elastic cuffs at wrists with thumb loops
distinctive_features: Single front kangaroo pocket—large enough for commute essentials, positioned for easy access while cycling
Packable hood with integrated drawcord storage in collar
Subtle Pelikan Technical Outerwear logo on shoulder (small, reflective, practical not decorative)
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 functional—solid mid-range technical wear. Quality and durability without luxury markup. Accessible to working professionals, educators, outdoor workers.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by urban cyclists, field researchers, teachers, commuters, and anyone navigating the GLMZ's brutal weather. Signals practical competence and familiarity with sustained rain. No status signal—just competence. Popular in academia and outdoor-adjacent work circles.
physical_description.condition_typical: Breaks in quickly with light use; develops subtle creases at elbows and shoulders. Remains pristine for years if maintained. Seams stay sealed. Hood shows minor packing wrinkles from daily stowing. No visible wear unless heavily used.
